title: Upper Colorado River flows in the warm water years 2019-2026 were below forecasts with flat temperature sensitivity in two of three frozen models; 2019-2024 alone did not separate the values
abstract: Published temperature sensitivities of Upper Colorado River flow range from -2.5 %/degC (Hoerling et al. 2019) to -9.3 %/degC (Milly and Dunne 2020). We did a forward test. We fitted models of USBR Lees Ferry natural flow on water years (WY) 1906-2018 with NOAA nClimGrid basin precipitation (P) and temperature (T). The sensitivity S was fixed at 0, -2.5, -6 or -9.3 %/degC, or was free. In the frozen plan test (WY2019-2024), all models over-predicted on average, but no S from -15 to +5 was rejected (p > 0.25 for the published values). After the plan, we added the very warm WY2025-2026 (WY2026 T +3.3 degC) with proxy natural flows from Reclamation 24-Month Study unregulated Powell inflow plus a 3.8 MAF offset (8.5 and 7.3 MAF). With October-March and April-September P, the mean 2019-2026 error rejected S flatter than -7.25 (z = -2.8 at -2.5; -1.5 at -9.3). With annual P, only S flatter than -1.75 was rejected. With previous-year P added, no published value was rejected. The free fit gave S = -9.7 (SE 1.9) for 1906-2018, but -14.0 (SE 2.3) for 1906-1962 and -4.3 (SE 2.9) for 1963-2018; all 19 upper-basin nodes were flatter after 1950. The low fitted P elasticity (about 1.2) agrees with early precipitation errors. Registered WY2026 forecasts were 9.0-12.4 MAF; the proxy is 7.3 MAF. Limitations: six frozen test years, a single extreme proxy year, provisional flows, model-form dependence and one climate data set. The evidence weakly favours sensitivities near -7 to -10 %/degC in the recent warm climate, but it does not identify one value.

B uses annual P; C uses October-March and April-September P.

z value of the mean log forecast error as a function of the fixed temperature sensitivity S for three model forms. Grey: frozen plan years WY2019-2024. Blue: WY2019-2026 with proxy flows. Orange: WY2026 alone. The shaded band is |z| < 1.96. Negative z means that the flow was below the forecast.
